content.text:
There's no fixed magic number, but for a kid Kit's age, most Canadian pediatric guidance focuses less on a strict hour count and more on balance and content quality — sleep, activity, and family time should come first, with screens fitting around them, not the other way around.

A few practical anchors that work well at 8:

- Set a weekend cap you both agree on ahead of time (many families land somewhere around 1–2 hours), so it's not a fresh negotiation every day.
- Keep screens out of the last hour before bed — it affects sleep quality.
- Prioritize active or social time first (outside play, family plans), then screen time as the "after" activity.

If Kit has specific behaviour issues tied to screens (meltdowns at cutoff, sleep trouble), that's worth flagging to your pediatric office — I can't speak to anything diagnostic there.
